newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazilian state to sell power company in October.
newsitem.headline: Brazilian state to sell power company in October.

text.p: The Brazilian state of Mato Grosso will sell its electrical power utility Cemat at a privatization auction in October, a consultant for the state said.
Oscar Salomao, director of Maxima Consultoria, told Reuters that proceeds from the sale of Cemat will be used to pay off part of the firm's debt to federal power utility Eletrobras.
Cemat has a net worth of 142 million reais and is heavily indebted, with debts totalling 600 million reais, he said.
The company's revenues are expected to rise 17 percent to 250 million this year from 213 million reais in 1996, Salomao said.
Cemat serves nearly 500,000 customers in the promising market of rural Mato Grosso state, where eletricity demand is growing at an annual rate of 18 percent, he added.
Mato Grosso is located in Brazil's largely unpopulated west-central region.
